data.hypothesis: Keep the existing factor-two target coarsening and reduce the block size from 256 to 64 threads, with 128 outputs per block. More, smaller CTAs may expose additional scheduling parallelism for the long source loops; launch overhead or occupancy effects could instead hurt, so no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: These factor-two measurements are relevant to launch-size tuning on the same frozen target, but do not establish why timings differ.
memory_lessons.claim: The factor-two 128-thread configuration measured 0.002617 s, while the factor-two 256-thread configuration measured 0.002727 s. Both were slower than the 0.001847 s baseline; the evidence does not establish a speedup over baseline or explain the block-size difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure factor-two coarsening with 64 threads and 128 outputs per block using the full correctness suite and official timing metric.

data.notes: The kernel remains unchanged: its two target indices are spaced by blockDim.x and its block base advances by 2 * blockDim.x, matching 128 outputs per 64-thread block. Shared-memory staging remains disabled. Supplied evidence contains no register-count or occupancy measurements; assess this candidate by controller results without inferring those metrics.
transformations: Retain factor-two target coarsening and set the block size to 64 threads.
Set items_per_block to 128 to match the kernel's two targets per thread; keep shared_memory_bytes at zero.
Leave the kernel bounds checks and self-interaction handling unchanged so arbitrary N remains covered.
